answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a wander as the anchor of the cost. A mesa stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a karst...
